subject: Post-call: throughput & streaming SLOs — proposed measurement and reporting
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <samira@finovate.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: throughput & streaming SLOs — proposed measurement and reporting

Hi Samira — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on SLO definition and what we need from Finovate to size and draft the SLA language.

Recap (short):
- Goal: production-grade inference with deterministic latency and predictable cost for your streaming product.
- Key knobs we covered: per-request latency targets, streaming TTFB/time-to-last-byte, concurrency (simultaneous open streams), and effective throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec under steady-state).

What we propose next (actionable):
1) Measurement definitions (first pass) — attached SLO-draft-v1.docx. Please review but main points below.
2) You to send representative traffic samples and a short summary of peak percentiles (samples per minute, session lengths) — Brent said he'd share a CSV of traffic samples.
3) Align on reporting cadence (weekly dashboard + monthly SLA report) and remedies (credits ladder) — see section 4 in the attachment.
4) Schedule a 30m follow-up to finalize measurement wording and confirm exclusions. I proposed times in the calendar link in Ben's note.

Quick summary of the measurement approach in the draft:
- Non-streaming endpoints: latency measured at server egress (time between request received by Redwood's edge and final token emitted to customer), primary metric p95 over 5-min rolling windows.
- Streaming endpoints: two metrics — time-to-first-byte (TTFB) for stream start and time-to-last-byte (TTLB) for completion for normal (non-cancelled) sessions; p95 across sessions over 1-hour windows.
- Concurrency: measured as number of simultaneously open streams per org/account, sampled every 10s and reported as p99 over 1h.
- Throughput: tokens/sec under steady-state (excluding ramp-up), and requests/sec for burst analysis.

Exclusions called out in the draft: scheduled maintenance windows, force majeure, customer-originated malformed inputs, customer-side network issues. We'll need your procurement/security teams to confirm acceptable exclusions.

Attachments: [SLO-draft-v1.docx] (short doc, sectioned for legal + ops wording)

If that looks reasonable I can loop in legal/procurement and have a near-final SLA for your procurement team by next week — contingent on the traffic sample Brent promised.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
--
Redwood Inference — developer-first inference for production

From: Samira Patel <samira@finovate.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Brent Lee <brent@streamhub.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: throughput & streaming SLOs — proposed measurement and reporting

Thanks Jordan — useful summary. Appreciate the draft. Attaching a small sample export (events-level) and a short note on session patterns.

Clarifications / constraints from our side:
- Typical session length: ~18–45s, median ~26s. Peak concurrent streams per org typically 120–160 during market open.
- Bursts: short spikes up to ~800 rps for 10–30s, then drop to 200–300 rps steady.
- For streaming we care most about TTFB (first tokens must be under 200ms p95) — TTLB is less critical but useful for tail analysis.
- On exclusions: we cannot accept broad "malformed input" exclusion without examples — our product sometimes sends large batched prompts. Can you specify size thresholds or rate limits that would constitute exclusion?

Attaching: [traffic-samples.csv]

We'll review the SLO wording but a few asks up front:
- Can you confirm whether p95 for streaming TTFB is measured server-side and excludes client-side aggregation/delay?
- Reporting cadence: weekly dashboards are good — can you include a weekly CSV export that we can ingest into our internal dashboards?

If you can update the doc to include explicit size/rate thresholds for exclusion and call out server-side measurement for TTFB, we can move quickly. I'm available next Tue/Thu afternoon if you want to lock a follow-up.

Thanks,
Samira Patel
Head of Product, Finovate AI

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <samira@finovate.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: throughput & streaming SLOs — proposed measurement and reporting

Samira — thanks for the traffic sample, very helpful. I pulled a few notes for the SLO language and proposed precise measurement wording we can insert into the draft. Pasting the key bits below so legal/procurement have minimal back-and-forth.

Proposed measurement definitions (concrete):
- Non-streaming latency (p95): measured at Redwood's egress point (timestamp when final response bytes depart Redwood's edge) minus ingress timestamp. Aggregation window: 5-minute rolling window. Reporting: hourly rollups and daily/weekly CSV exports.
- Streaming TTFB (p95): measured from Redwood's ingress timestamp to time when first token bytes are emitted to the client stream by Redwood's gateway. For clarity: we do not include client-side buffering, network re-ordering, or browser-level rendering delays. Aggregation window: 1-hour sampling; SLA evaluated using p95 over a 30-day calendar period.
- Streaming TTLB: for sessions that complete normally (not client-cancelled), TTLB p95 reported as an optional diagnostic metric, not a primary SLA metric.
- Concurrency: number of concurrently open streams per account sampled every 10s; concurrency SLO defined as p99 over a 1-hour window.
- Throughput: tokens/sec measured at model execution point; supplemental request/sec measured at gateway for burst detection. Steady-state throughput computed excluding initial 20s of session start for streaming to avoid ramp artifacts.

Exclusions (we can be explicit):
- Scheduled maintenance (>= 30m notice)
- Force majeure and third-party cloud provider outages (documented status pages)
- Customer-originated malformed requests: defined as requests that exceed 1MB payload or contain >50k tokens after client-side preprocessing, OR requests that exceed agreed rate limits (a per-account token/sec threshold we set in the provisioning sheet).
- Customer network failures (e.g., TCP resets from client IP ranges) — we log these as part of diagnostic reports and exclude from SLA calculations when corroborated by TCP-level traces.

Reporting & remedies:
- Monthly SLA report (PDF + CSV): includes p95/p99 tables for the month, incident list, and sample traces for any claimed breach.
- Weekly dashboard: near-real-time metrics + downloadable CSV for ingestion.
- Remedies: tiered service credit schedule tied to % of monthly p95 breaches for measurement windows. Example: 
  - <0.1% monthly breach: no credits
  - 0.1–1%: 5% of monthly invoice for affected routes
  - >1%: 15% of monthly invoice for affected routes
We can make the exact credit ladder procurement-friendly; this is a starting point.

Operational asks from Finovate to make the SLA practical:
- Confirm the per-account concurrency ceiling you expect for Reserved/Dedicated or whether you want us to recommend tiers.
- Confirm acceptable maximum payload size or allow us to set a default that triggers exclusion language.

Next steps: I added three calendar slots (Tue 10/20 11:00–11:30 PT, Tue 10/20 15:00–15:30 PT, Thu 10/22 09:00–09:30 PT). Please pick one and I'll get an invite out. I'll also update SLO-draft-v1 with the explicit malformed-request thresholds and the measurement wording above.

Attachments referenced: SLO-draft-v1.docx (will be updated), sample traces available upon request.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Samira Patel <samira@finovate.ai>

Cc: Brent Lee <brent@streamhub.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: throughput & streaming SLOs — proposed measurement and reporting

Ben/Jordan — this is great and much clearer. Quick replies:
- The proposed malformed-request thresholds (1MB / 50k tokens) are acceptable. We will flag any legitimate batched payloads in advance so they are treated as "approved large requests" and not excluded.
- We confirm we need the TTFB p95 objective at 200ms for streaming for the first 90 days post-launch; after that we will evaluate whether a tighter target is needed. Can you add a launch-period clause to the SLA draft?
- Reporting cadence and the monthly credit ladder look fine as a starting point; legal may ask for more conservative credit percentages, but the structure is what matters.

I'll take the Tue 10/20 11:00 PT slot. Please send the invite and an updated SLO doc before then (even a redline is fine). Also please share the weekly CSV schema so our analytics team can map fields.

Thanks — will loop in procurement if needed after the doc update.

Samira Patel
Head of Product, Finovate AI
